players.product: inspection & metrology for HBM / 2.5D advanced packaging

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 AND FULL-YEAR 2025 RESULTS (call; CEO Rafi Amit had lost his voice, so COO Ramy Langer gave the opening remarks): CFO Moshe Eisenberg said Q4 revenue was a record $128.1 million, up 9% from Q4 2024. Gross margin was 51.1% and operating margin 28.6%. Net income was $40.7 million, or $0.81 per diluted share. Full-year 2025 revenue was $496.9 million, up 16%, with a 51.6% gross margin and a 30% operating margin. The COO called this Camtek's "milestone of $0.5 billion in revenues". FY2025 mix: "approximately 50% was driven by AI-related products, 20% came from the other advanced packaging applications". CMOS image sensors, compound semiconductors, front-end and general 2D applications made up the rest.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 revenue $128.1 million (+9% YoY); gross margin 51.1%; operating margin 28.6%; EPS $0.81; FY2025 revenue $496.9 million (+16%), gross margin 51.6%, operating margin 30%; approximately 50% AI-related, 20% other advanced packaging

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 OUTLOOK (point-in-time guidance): Q1 2026 revenue is guided to around $120 million. Management expects growth in Q2 and "more significant growth in the second half of 2026". The COO said the months since the previous guidance "significantly reinforced our confidence" in the second half, and "we expect 2026 to be another double-digit growth year for Camtek". Management said the slow start reflects the timing of customer orders: "big part of their capacity expansion and especially the big ones is planned for the second half". Asked about Q3 versus Q4, the COO said the step-up comes in the second half and the exact quarter depends on the customer. The CFO guided first-half gross margin between 50.5% to 51.5%, improving in the second half as revenue grows. This follows bill-of-materials and supply-chain measures. OpEx is expected to rise in the first half on R&D investment.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 2026 revenue guidance around $120 million; 2026 expected to be another double-digit growth year, second-half weighted; H1 gross margin 50.5% to 51.5%, improving in H2

quarterly_data.signal: HAWK ORDERS FROM A FAB-BUILDING IDM: The COO said 2026 growth "is largely linked to the pace of which device manufacturers, particularly memory suppliers plan to expand their production capacity". As an example, Camtek announced "a $25 million order received from an IDM customer for multiple Hawk systems". Earlier orders from the same customer in recent months bring its total "to approximately $45 million". The customer is not named. It "continues to expand its manufacturing capacity by building new fabs to meet growing demand for components produced for AI applications", and Camtek expects more orders from it. Customers have also been checking Camtek's "ability to ship and install a double-digit number of systems within a relatively short time frame". Management expects other major customers to expand capacity as well.
quarterly_data.figure: $25 million IDM order for multiple Hawk systems; approximately $45 million total from this customer in recent months

quarterly_data.signal: HBM4 TRANSITION = MORE METROLOGY/INSPECTION: The COO said "The transition to HBM4 is already in process, and represents a major opportunity for us. We are the tool of reference for 3D metrology at all major players." Camtek has "a significant market share in 2D inspection, which we expect to expand in 2026". HBM4 has "a lot more dense structures", and it "is more metrology and inspection intensive". He expects the industry to move gradually to HBM4. On tool choice, customers making the higher HBM generations ("the 4 and the 5") will, "to a certain extent, use the Hawk". Camtek already has "many hundreds of Eagles" doing HBM work, but "some of the future capacity that will be built will be more tended towards the Hawk".

HAWK / EAGLE GEN 5 PLATFORM MIX: Both models launched about a year ago, and Camtek has "already installed dozens of systems of each over the past year". The COO said "the Hawk and the G5 accounted to about 30% of our revenues this year. We expect it to be at least 50% in 2026." The Hawk targets high-end work: very large bump counts ("150 million and more") with shallow bumps, applications heading to 100 nanometers, front-end-related work and customers who later want to use the tool for hybrid bonding. The G5 is "very popular in the OSATs world" for its flexibility, accuracy and ROI. Camtek has also finished developing new capabilities for customers' next-generation products and has shown them to several customers, with "strong validation and interest".
quarterly_data.figure: Hawk and G5 about 30% of 2025 revenues; at least 50% expected in 2026

quarterly_data.signal: COWOS-LIKE PACKAGING MOVING TO OSATs: The COO said "we see what is called the CoWoS technology, moving to OSAT". OSATs are Camtek's "home ground", with "hundreds of machines" there. OSATs are "about 50% of our business". They keep investing in advanced packaging and "are starting to adapt the CoWoS of the AI technologies, and this is for real". Camtek says it "already have POs on hand. We have in the backlog." He agreed that 2026 should bring strong growth at IDMs (HBM exposure), OSATs and foundries (2.5D). He called advanced-packaging market growth (led by Fan-Out and bump inspection) "definitely double digits" but gave no exact number. China, mostly OSAT sales, is expected to be "stable"; management does not see "any signs of weakness". No named OSAT customers were given.
quarterly_data.figure: OSATs about 50% of business; advanced packaging market growth double digits

quarterly_data.signal: CAPACITY NOT A CONSTRAINT: The COO said "at this stage, we don't have limitation on our current capacity". Process changes and efficiency gains have lifted revenue capacity: "I think it is well over $700 million in capacity." Camtek has also started expanding: "we will have additional capacity in Europe. I believe it will happen late '26". The CFO added "we do have the capacity, we have the inventory and all the supply chain ready for the growth". The COO said Camtek can meet demand whether 2026 growth lands "very high teens or mid-teens", with "enough buffers in place".
quarterly_data.figure: revenue capacity well over $700 million; additional capacity in Europe expected late '26

quarterly_data.signal: VISIBILITY INTO 2027 AND MARKET SHARE: The COO said "we're starting to see also signs of '27". This is not yet backlog, but "customers are talking to us about shipping machines in the first and second quarter of '27" and are putting in "some initial numbers". Compared with a quarter earlier, Camtek has "much better visibility" from new orders and a stronger pipeline, and understands "the timing of the expected orders". On competition for HBM sockets: "We have not lost any market share to competitors. We also estimate that we will be able to increase our market share this year". It expects to do this by entering more inspection and metrology steps. Some steps are already confirmed and shipping, and others are in customer validation.

CASH AND WORKING CAPITAL: The CFO said cash and cash equivalents, including short- and long-term deposits and marketable securities, were $851.1 million on December 31, 2025, versus $794 million at the end of Q3. Q4 cash generation from operations was a very strong $61.2 million, driven by collections and lower inventory. Accounts receivable fell to $90.8 million, and days sales outstanding dropped to 65 days from 81. Inventory is "down by $50 million" after the build-up for the Hawk and Eagle Gen 5 launch. By geography, Asia was 89% of Q4 revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: cash and investments $851.1 million; Q4 cash from operations $61.2 million; inventory down by $50 million; DSO 65 days; Asia 89% of Q4 revenue

contracts.signal: The COO named TSMC as a customer: "When we talk about the HBM, when we talk about the CoWoS, we talk about TSMC. All of these are our customers". On the chiplet business he added: "TSMC made a note -- made a comment in one of the previous announcements that Camtek is a significant vendor to them. So it's not a secret. Yes, we are there. We have a share of the chiplet business. We are doing a few steps there." He said this covers "not only one step, it's multiple steps". Camtek expects to gain share in chiplets too. He did not give a revenue figure or name the specific steps.
